6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartTwistSplit
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.DegreeBaseFieldInvariance
8	
9	/-!
10	# COV-1 input 2: the DEGREE of the presenting class of the twisted fibre class
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean` names the Čech class that presents the twisted fibre class
13	over the splitting field `L`:
14	
15	  `M₀ · CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z)`.
16	
17	`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 2–4 then need its `L`-degree, because that is what decides whether the
18	class can carry an effective witness with `h¹ = 0` at all: the greedy drop of
19	`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean` consumes a divisor of degree `g + e`.
20	
21	This file computes it, and the computation is exactly the degree ledger the worksheet pins:
22	
23	  `classDeg L (presenting class) = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`   when `λ` is degree-zero,
24	
25	so under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g` it is `+g` — and with the drop budget
26	`e` folded in (`deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g − e`) it is `g + e`, which is `exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`'s
27	hypothesis on the nose.
28	
29	## The two halves, and which one is nontrivial
30	
31	* the **twist factor** is a base class base-changed to `L`, so its `L`-degree is its
32	  `k`-degree by **E-iv-alg** (`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`) — no per-field
33	  ledger constant crosses, which is the I-0204 discipline;
34	* the **`λ` factor** has `L`-degree zero, and this is where degree-zero-ness is *spent*.
35	  It is `degAt λ (testPoint) = 0` read through the degree seam: `degAt` of a class whose
36	  affine collapse is a plus unit of `relPicMk M₀` is `classDeg` of `M₀`
37	  (`degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk`).
38	
39	The second half is the reason this file exists rather than being three `rw`s inside COV-1: the
40	seam from "`μ` is presented over `L` by `M₀`" to "`classDeg L M₀ = degAt μ`" is a statement
41	about `PicEtAff.map` versus `picEtMap`, not about degrees.
42	
43	## Main declarations
44	
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_cechPicMap_base_of_field` — the `L`-degree of a base class
46	  base-changed to `L` is its `k`-degree (E-iv-alg in the `relCurveMap` spelling).
47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange` — the twist factor contributes
48	  exactly `m·d₁ − deg_k Z`.
49	-/
50	
51	set_option autoImplicit false
52	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
53	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
54	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
55	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
56	
57	universe u
58	
59	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
60	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
61	
62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
63	
64	open AlgebraicJacobian
65	
66	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
67	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
68	
69	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
70	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
71	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
72	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
73	
74	noncomputable section
75	
76	/-! ## E-iv-alg in the `relCurveMap` spelling -/
77	
78	variable (C) in
79	/-- **The degree of a base class is base-field invariant** — E-iv-alg
80	(`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`) read along `relCurveMap C k L` rather than along
81	the raw whisker.  The two agree by `relCurveMap_eq_overSpecMap_ofId`, and this is the spelling
82	every chart-layer statement uses. -/
83	theorem classDeg_cechPicMap_base_of_field (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
84	    (Λ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic) :
85	    classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left) Λ)
86	      = classDeg k Λ :=
87	  classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition C (Algebra.ofId k L) Λ
88	
89	variable (C) in
90	/-- **The twist factor's contribution to the degree**: `m·d₁ − deg_k Z`, computed at the
91	splitting field but equal to a `k`-level quantity — the point of routing it through E-iv-alg
92	rather than through a per-field ledger. -/
93	theorem classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] (m : ℕ)
94	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
95	    classDeg L (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left)
96	        (chartTwistClass C m Z))
97	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
98	  rw [classDeg_cechPicMap_base_of_field C L]
99	  change classDeg k (thetaCechClass C ^ m * (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass k Z)⁻¹) = _
100	  rw [classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, classDeg_pow, classDeg_picClass]
101	  ring
102	
103	/-! ## Where degree-zero-ness is spent: the `λ` factor -/
104	
105	variable (C) in
106	/-- **The presenting class's `classDeg` equals the transported plus-class degree.**
107	
108	`classDeg L M = degAff L (PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν))`, whenever `M` presents
109	`ν` over `L`.  Read the statement, not the ambition: the right-hand side is the plus-class
110	degree **at `L`**, and this is `degAff_unit` plus `relPicDeg_relPicMk`, nothing more.
111	
112	**A CORRECTION, and it is the reason this docstring is now shorter than it was** (issue I-0614,
113	found by fresh-context review).  The previous version claimed this theorem was the `w4-datb`
114	§1.2 step-2 seam — that it carried `degAt ν = 0` over to `classDeg M = 0` — and justified the
115	`K → L` step by citing `degAff_map_eq`.  **No such lemma exists**: the only occurrence of that
116	name in the workspace was that docstring.  So the claim was a phantom citation, and the step it
117	claimed to make is genuinely absent:
118	
119	* what the coverage argument HAS is `degAt ν t = degAff K (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)`, at `K`;
120	* what this theorem's RHS mentions is `degAff L (PicEtAff.map C L …)`, at `L`;
121	* nothing in the tree equates them.  The missing brick is **base-field invariance of `degAff`
122	  under `PicEtAff.map`**, a small real lemma shaped like the landed `degAff_baseFieldShuffle`
123	  (`Picard/Pic0ThetaAssembly.lean:67`) — measured, not guessed: `exact?` on
124	  `degAff L (map C L a) = degAff K a` finds nothing.
125	
126	**STEP 2 IS NOW DISCHARGED (2026-07-28), and this paragraph's "NOT discharged" is superseded.**
127	The missing `degAff` invariance was proved as `PicEtAff.degAff_map`
128	(`Picard/DegreeZeroBaseField.lean`) — and it needs *no* hypothesis on `L/K` at all, not even
129	finiteness, so it is weaker-premised than the `degAff_baseFieldShuffle` shape predicted above.
130	Step 2 itself is `classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff` / `classDeg_presenting_eq_zero`
131	(`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`), which reaches `classDeg L M = degAff K a`
132	directly and therefore does **not** route through this theorem.
133	
134	This theorem is kept because it is true and was the first half of the seam, but it remains
135	without consumers: the landed route reads the `K`-side degree rather than the `L`-side one, so
136	its `PicEtAff.map`-shaped right-hand side is no longer the useful spelling.
137	
138	The other half of the ledger — the twist factor's contribution — IS complete
139	(`classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange` above, via E-iv-alg). -/
140	theorem classDeg_of_presenting {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
141	    (ν : picEt C (overSpec k K)) {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L]
142	    [IsScalarTower k K L] (M : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CechPic)
143	    (hM : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)
144	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)) :
145	    classDeg L M = PicEtAff.degAff L (PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K ν)) := by
146	  rw [hM, PicEtAff.degAff_unit, relPicDeg_relPicMk]
147	
148	end
149	
150	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageDegree
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DegreeZeroBaseField
8	
9	/-!
10	# COV-1 / `w4-datb` §1.2 STEP 2, DISCHARGED
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegree.lean` computes the twist factor's contribution to the degree
13	of the presenting class and then states plainly (issue I-0614) that the `λ` factor's
14	contribution is *not* discharged: the coverage argument holds `degAt λ t` at the fibre field
15	`K`, the presenting class `M₀` lives over the splitting field `L`, and nothing in the tree
16	equated the two readings.
17	
18	`Picard/DegreeZeroBaseField.lean` supplies exactly the missing equation
19	(`PicEtAff.degAff_map`, unconditional in `L/K`).  This file spends it, so that step 2 becomes
20	a landed theorem rather than a named gap, and then assembles the full degree ledger of the
21	presenting class of the TWISTED fibre class — which is what `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean`
22	takes as its hypothesis `hdeg`.
23	
24	## The ledger, in one line
25	
26	For `λ` degree-zero at the fibre point and `M` presenting the twisted class over `L`:
27	
28	  `classDeg L M = 0 + (m·d₁ − deg_k Z) = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`,
29	
30	so the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g − e` makes it `g + e`, which is
31	`exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`'s hypothesis on the nose.  **No per-field ledger constant
32	crosses a base-field boundary** (the I-0204 discipline): `d₁ = classDeg k Θ` is read at `k`
33	and reaches `L` by E-iv-alg, while the `λ` factor's contribution is *zero*, which transports
34	trivially.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff` — **step 2**: the `L`-degree of a class
39	  presenting a plus class over `K` is that plus class's degree at `K`.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_presenting_eq_zero` — the degree-zero case, the form the
41	  coverage argument spends.
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_presenting_twist` — **the assembled ledger**: the `L`-degree of
43	  the presenting class of the twisted fibre class of a degree-zero `λ`.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_presenting_twist_eq_add` — the same under the chart-index
45	  constraint, delivered in the `g + e` shape `Pic0ChartCoverageFibre` consumes.
46	-/
47	
48	set_option autoImplicit false
49	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
50	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
51	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
52	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

54	universe u
55	
56	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
57	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
58	
59	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
60	
61	open AlgebraicJacobian
62	
63	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
64	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
65	
66	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
67	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
68	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
69	
70	noncomputable section
71	
72	/-! ## Step 2 itself -/
73	
74	variable (C) in
75	/-- **COV-1 / `w4-datb` §1.2 step 2** — the seam I-0614 recorded as absent, now landed.
76	
77	If the plus class `a` over the fibre field `K` is presented over an extension `L` by the Čech
78	class `M`, then `classDeg L M` is `a`'s own degree at `K`.
79	
80	Both halves are one rewrite each: the `L`-side reading of the unit is `classDeg L M`
81	(`degAff_unit` + `relPicDeg_relPicMk`), and the base-field step is `PicEtAff.degAff_map`.  The
82	substance is entirely in that second lemma — and note what it does *not* require: `L/K` is an
83	arbitrary field extension here, not a finite separable one, so a consumer may present its class
84	over whatever extension the splitting produced. -/
85	theorem classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
86	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
87	    (a : PicEtAff C K) (M : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CechPic)
88	    (hM : PicEtAff.map C L a = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)) :
89	    classDeg L M = PicEtAff.degAff K a := by
90	  rw [← PicEtAff.degAff_map L a, hM, PicEtAff.degAff_unit, relPicDeg_relPicMk]
91	
92	variable (C) in
93	/-- **Step 2 at a degree-zero class** — the form the coverage argument spends.
94	
95	`degAt λ t = 0` is exactly what membership of `pic0Subgroup` gives at the fibre point, and the
96	plus-class degree of the restricted class is `degAt` by definition; so a presenting class of a
97	degree-zero fibre class has `classDeg L = 0` over **any** extension it is presented over. -/
98	theorem classDeg_presenting_eq_zero {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
99	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T)
100	    (hlam : degAt lam t = 0)
101	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
102	    (M : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CechPic)
103	    (hM : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
104	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)) :
105	    classDeg L M = 0 := by
106	  rw [classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff C L _ M hM]
107	  exact hlam
108	
109	/-! ## The assembled ledger of the twisted class -/
110	
111	variable (C) in
112	/-- **The degree of the presenting class of the TWISTED fibre class** (`w4-datb` §1.2
113	steps 2–4, assembled).
114	
115	For a class `lam` whose fibre degree at `t` vanishes, presented over `L` by `M₀`, the twisted
116	presenting class of `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean` has
117	
118	  `classDeg L (M₀ · CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
119	      = m · classDeg k Θ − deg_k Z`.
120	
121	The two factors come from opposite sides and neither carries a per-field constant across a
122	base-field boundary: the twist factor is read at `k` and transported by E-iv-alg
123	(`classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange`), and the `λ` factor contributes `0`
124	(`classDeg_presenting_eq_zero`). -/
125	theorem classDeg_presenting_twist {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
126	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T)
127	    (hlam : degAt lam t = 0)
128	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
129	    (M₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CechPic)
130	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
131	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
132	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
133	    classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map
134	        ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
135	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z := by
136	  rw [classDeg_mul, classDeg_presenting_eq_zero C lam t hlam L M₀ hM₀,
137	    classDeg_chartTwistClass_baseChange C L m Z, zero_add]
138	
139	variable (C) in
140	/-- **The ledger in the `g + e` shape** — the hypothesis `Pic0ChartCoverageFibre`'s
141	`exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` asks for (`hdeg`).
142	
143	Under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g − e` (the drop budget `e` folded into the
144	chart index), the presenting class of the twisted fibre class has degree exactly `g + e`.  This
145	is where the chart index is *paid for*: the constraint is a hypothesis, because per `w4-datb`
146	§0.2.2 / I-0204 the exponent `m` must be chosen against the fibre's OWN vanishing bound and no
147	uniform choice exists. -/
148	theorem classDeg_presenting_twist_eq_add {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
149	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T)
150	    (hlam : degAt lam t = 0)
151	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
152	    (M₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CechPic)
153	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
154	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
155	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (g e : ℕ)
156	    (hZ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
157	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (g : ℤ) - (e : ℤ)) :
158	    classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map
159	        ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
160	      = (g : ℤ) + e := by
161	  rw [classDeg_presenting_twist C lam t hlam L M₀ hM₀ m Z, hZ]
162	  ring
163	
164	end
165	
166	end AlgebraicGeometry

The description of step 2 as "*the* honest content" is right that it is not bookkeeping and
wrong that it is a single obligation.  `IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` conjoins **relative
representability** (the fibre product is a scheme at all) with **the property clause** (each
represented pullback is an open immersion).  The GAP-2/classifier story is the input to the
second only.  The first needs just an open of the test, and `chartLocus` is one
unconditionally — so it is not CERT-Σ-gated at all.

That split is landed: `Picard/Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean` (the criterion, from
elementwise data) and `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean` (instantiated at the Abel chart,
reducing the datum from four fields to three).  `IsChartUniv` below is unchanged as a
*statement* — it is still the right pin — but it is no longer the right unit of *pricing*.
Read `isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre` for what a lane now actually owes.

8	/-!
9	# THE ATLAS IS CHART-PARAMETER HETEROGENEOUS — each chart may carry its own `n`
10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` establishes that at a chart index legal at parameter
12	`n` the coverage theorem's threshold is forced to equal `n`, and that at `n = g` the resulting
13	hypothesis is false.  Both that file and the review it adjudicates (I-0660) then reason about
14	"the" chart parameter, as though the atlas had one.
15	
16	**It does not, and this file proves it.**  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
17	(`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) takes a family `f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ pic0SigmaSheaf`
18	indexed by an arbitrary `ι`, with `X : ι → Scheme` and a *per-index* certificate
19	`hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i)`.  Nothing ties the `X i` together, so nothing ties
20	their chart parameters together either: `mixedParamChart` below builds such a family from a
21	per-index parameter `nn : ι → ℕ`, a per-index representation of `divFunctor C π (nn i)`, and a
22	per-index chart index legal *at that index's own parameter*.
23	
24	## Why this matters, and it changes the shape of the residue
25	
26	The `b = n` calibration is per-chart.  So the question "can coverage use DAT-0a's threshold?"
27	does not have to be answered uniformly: a point whose splitting field has threshold `b_L` can be
28	covered by *the chart whose parameter is `b_L.toNat`*, and a different point by a different
29	chart.  The I-0204 non-uniformity of `m` — no single exponent works for every fibre — is
30	therefore **not** an obstruction to the atlas; it is an argument for an atlas indexed by the
31	threshold, which is what a heterogeneous family is.
32	
33	What this does **not** do, and the honest limit of the observation:
34	
35	* it does not produce the representations.  `mixedParamChart` takes `rep i` as a hypothesis, one
36	  per parameter, and the divisor-representability lane supplies `divFunctor C π g` — a single
37	  parameter.  So the heterogeneous atlas is *admissible* but not yet *inhabited* beyond `n = g`;
38	* it does not discharge `IsChartUniv` at any index (still CERT-Σ-gated, `Pic0ChartPair.lean`);
39	* it says nothing about local surjectivity, which is DAT-B B-6 and is what would actually consume
40	  the freedom.
41	
42	So the correct statement of the residue, refining `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`'s: **B-5's step 3
43	is a question about which parameters `divFunctor C π n` is representable at, not about
44	reconciling one parameter with one threshold.**  If representability is available only at `n = g`
45	then the slack must go into `Z` (and its legality is open, as recorded there); if it is available
46	at every `n`, coverage can be assembled chart-by-chart against each fibre's own threshold and the
47	`b = n` forcing is harmless.  That is a sharper question than either prior reading, and it is
48	addressed to the divRep lane rather than to this one.
49	
50	## Main declarations
51	
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamChart` — a chart family with a per-index chart parameter.
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart` — its `hf` clause is exactly a
54	  per-index `IsChartUniv`, so heterogeneity costs nothing in the certificate.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mixedParamRepresentableBy` — such a family is admissible input to
56	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  **This is the whole point**: the DAT-glue seam never sees a
57	  chart parameter.
58	-/

87	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
89	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
90	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
91	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
92	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
93	    yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme.{u})) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
94	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)

98	family is exactly a per-index `IsChartUniv`, by definition of both.
99	
100	So a lane that can discharge CHART-U(c) *at one parameter* can discharge it index-by-index at
101	different parameters, with no additional compatibility between them — there is no coherence
102	condition across indices, because `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` imposes none. -/
103	theorem isOpenImmersion_presheaf_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
104	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
105	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
106	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
107	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
108	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
109	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
110	    (huniv : ∀ i, IsChartUniv C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) (V i)) (i : ι) :
111	    IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i) :=
112	  huniv i

115	/-- **A mixed-parameter chart family is admissible input to the DAT-glue seam.**
116	
117	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` accepts it verbatim.  This is the statement that settles the
118	question `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack` and I-0660 both left implicit: the representability engine
119	never sees a chart parameter, so the forced calibration `b = n` is a *per-chart* condition and
120	carries no uniformity obligation.

122	Note what remains hypothetical here and is not weakened by this: `hf` (i.e. `IsChartUniv`, still
123	CERT-Σ-gated), local surjectivity (DAT-B B-6), and the *existence* of `rep i` at parameters other
124	than `g` — which is the question this observation hands to the divisor-representability lane. -/
125	def mixedParamRepresentableBy {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
126	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
127	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
128	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
129	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
130	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
131	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
132	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i))
133	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
134	      (Sigma.desc (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))] :
135	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
136	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
137	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
138	  pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hf
139

23	
24	`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
25	"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
26	`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
27	degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
28	*membership of the locus* needs.
29	
30	The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
31	properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with

36	
37	So the feedback of step 6 was an artefact of routing coverage through the drop.  Cut the drop
38	and there is one `Z` again — the chart index's — and nothing to feed back.

10	
11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean` runs `w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–6 at a splitting field and
12	produces `IsSplitWitness` of a twisted class over `overSpec k L`.  The coverage theorem
13	(§1.2's `pic0_chartLocus_cover`) is a statement about a point `t` of a **general test** `T`:
14	
15	```
16	∃ c : ChartIndex C, t ∈ chartLocus c lam
17	```
18	
19	This file closes the gap between the two, which is one substitution and one collapse:
20	
21	* the fibre class at `t` is `picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam`, a class over the field
22	  `κ(t)` — so the fibre step applies at `K := κ(t)` with no change;

14	concluded that its `hb` "cannot be DAT-0a's threshold" and that step 3 is therefore not

16	settles which parts stand.**
17	
18	## What is confirmed, and it is a real correction to this lane's prose
19	
20	`ledger_forces_b_eq_n` reproduces the reviewer's derivation and generalises it: at a chart index
21	legal at parameter `n` — i.e. satisfying the constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − n` that
22	`chartValueTrans` / `chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:382`) require — the
23	hypothesis `hdeg` of `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` **determines `b`**, and `b = n`.  So
24	`b` is *not* a free parameter that DAT-0a may instantiate: the chart index pins it.
25	
26	`hb_forces_h0_eq_one` then shows what `hb` at `b = n` amounts to on a genus-`g` curve at `n = g`:
27	**every** degree-`g` divisor has `h⁰ = 1`.  That is false on any curve with a degree-`g`
28	effective divisor moving in a positive-dimensional family, and it is strictly stronger than
29	every threshold theorem in the tree (DAT-0a's bound is `n₁·deg F + 1 − χ = n₁·deg F + g` with
30	`0 < deg F`, so it exceeds `g` as soon as `n₁ ≥ 1`).  The reviewer's reading of the *strength*
31	is therefore confirmed, and sharpened: it is not merely "stronger than a threshold result", it
32	is a statement the χ-ledger converts into an `h⁰` equality for every divisor at once.
33	
34	## What does NOT follow — and this is the correction to the reviewer
35	
36	The reviewer's conclusion assumes `n = g`.  **`n` is a free parameter of the entire chart
37	layer.**  `divFunctor C π n`, `chartValue C π n m Z`, `chartValueTrans C π n m Z hdeg` and
38	`abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg` are all stated for an arbitrary `n : ℕ`; nothing in
39	`Pic0AtlasFromDivRep.lean` or `DivSchemeAbel.lean` pins it.  `n = g` is where the *divisor
40	representability lane* instantiates (`divFunctor_representableBy_of_chartClause`,
41	`DivRepAffPullClause.lean:475`), and where `Pic^0` has the right dimension — but the coverage
42	theorem does not know that.
43	
44	So `b = n` is a **calibration equation between two independently chosen numbers**, and reading
45	it as "an over-constraint" versus "the definition of the chart parameter" depends entirely on
46	which of `n` and `b` is free.  `index_of_threshold` records the direction that is actually
47	available: given DAT-0a's threshold `b ≥ 0` at the splitting field, a chart index constraint at
48	parameter `b.toNat` makes `hdeg` hold **by construction**.  There is no obstruction to
49	satisfying `hdeg`; the obstruction is that satisfying it *at n = g* requires the sharp
50	vanishing.

67	   legality (`0 ≤ Σ`) is the open question.

variable {A : Type u'} [Category.{v'} A] {FA : A → A → Type*} {CA : A → Type w'}
variable [∀ X Y, FunLike (FA X Y) (CA X) (CA Y)] [ConcreteCategory.{w'} A FA]

namespace Presheaf

/-- Given `f : F ⟶ G`, a morphism between presieves, and `s : G.obj (op U)`, this is the sieve
of `U` consisting of the `i : V ⟶ U` such that `s` restricted along `i` is in the image of `f`. -/
@[simps -isSimp]
def imageSieve {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) {U : C} (s : ToType (G.obj (op U))) : Sieve U where
  arrows V i := ∃ t : ToType (F.obj (op V)), f.app _ t = G.map i.op s
  downward_closed := by
    rintro V W i ⟨t, ht⟩ j
    refine ⟨F.map j.op t, ?_⟩
    rw [op_comp, G.map_comp, ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← ht, NatTrans.naturality_apply f]

lemma pullback_imageSieve
/-- A morphism of presheaves `f : F ⟶ G` is locally surjective with respect to a Grothendieck
topology if every section of `G` is locally in the image of `f`. -/
class IsLocallySurjective {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) : Prop where
  imageSieve_mem {U : C} (s : ToType (G.obj (op U))) : imageSieve f s ∈ J U

lemma imageSieve_mem {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) [IsLocallySurjective J f] {U : Cᵒᵖ}
    (s : ToType (G.obj U)) : imageSieve f s ∈ J U.unop :=
  IsLocallySurjective.imageSieve_mem _

instance {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) [IsLocallySurjective J f] :
    IsLocallySurjective J (whiskerRight f (forget A)) where
  imageSieve_mem s := imageSieve_mem J f s

theorem isLocallySurjective_iff_range_sheafify_eq_top {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsLocallySurjective J f ↔ (Subfunctor.range (whiskerRight f (forget A))).sheafify J = ⊤ := by
  simp only [Subfunctor.ext_iff, funext_iff, Set.ext_iff, Subfunctor.top_obj,
    Set.top_eq_univ, Set.mem_univ, iff_true]
  exact ⟨fun H _ => H.imageSieve_mem, fun H => ⟨H _⟩⟩

theorem isLocallySurjective_iff_range_sheafify_eq_top' {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsLocallySurjective J f ↔ (Subfunctor.range f).sheafify J = ⊤ := by
  apply isLocallySurjective_iff_range_sheafify_eq_top

theorem isLocallySurjective_iff_whisker_forget {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) :
    IsLocallySurjective J f ↔ IsLocallySurjective J (whiskerRight f (forget A)) := by
  simp only [isLocallySurjective_iff_range_sheafify_eq_top]
  rfl

theorem isLocallySurjective_of_surjective {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G)
    (H : ∀ U, Function.Surjective (f.app U)) : IsLocallySurjective J f where
  imageSieve_mem {U} s := by
    obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := H _ s
    rw [imageSieve_app]
    exact J.top_mem _

instance isLocallySurjective_of_iso {F G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ A} (f : F ⟶ G) [IsIso f] :
    IsLocallySurjective J f := by
  apply isLocallySurjective_of_surjective
  intro U

/-!
# DAT-B B-6: the local-surjectivity half of the `(f, hf)` handoff

`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` (`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161`) needs two things beyond the
charts: the `hf` certificate (C9b, reduced in `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`) and the

```
[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]
```

which is dat-b row B-6.  Three files carry that instance as a `variable`
(`JacobianDataCharts.lean:117`, `JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:183`,
`JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:131`) and **nothing anywhere produces one**.  This file supplies
the producer, in the form that DAT-B's coverage statement can actually feed.

## What local surjectivity unfolds to, and why that matters here

Mathlib's `Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective J f` has a single field: for every object `T` and
every section `s` of the target at `T`, the *image sieve* of `s` — the sieve of maps
`g : T' ⟶ T` along which `s` pulls back into the image of `f` — is a covering sieve.

For the Zariski topology on schemes that is exactly the geometric statement dat-b row B-5
proves: **every degree-zero class on a test is, locally on that test, a chart value**.  So
B-6 is not a further geometric obligation on top of B-5 — it is B-5 phrased against
mathlib's sieve-theoretic interface, plus the bookkeeping that turns a family of charts into
`Sigma.desc`.

The bookkeeping is what this file provides, and it is not trivial: the section must be hit
by *some* chart of the family, and `Sigma.desc` must be shown to see it.  That is
`ChartsCoverLocally` below.

## The honest scope, stated up front

`ChartsCoverLocally` is the hypothesis, not a theorem.  Its content is B-5 and B-5's residue
is recorded on the dat-b roadmap row (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation).  What
this file establishes is that **nothing else** stands between B-5 and the instance the
producer needs — in particular no compatibility across charts, because `Sigma.desc` has
none to check.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.ChartsCoverLocally` — the coverage hypothesis, stated exactly as the
  image sieve of `Sigma.desc` being covering, but spelled in terms of the individual charts
  so a producer never has to reason about the coproduct.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` — **B-6**: that hypothesis gives the
  instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective` — the degenerate sufficient
  condition (a chart that is surjective on points of every test already covers), recorded so
  the hypothesis is visibly *satisfiable* and not a disguised falsehood.
-/

set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

variable (C) in
/-- **The coverage hypothesis of DAT-B, stated per chart rather than on the coproduct.**

For every test `T` and every degree-zero class `s` on it, the maps into `T` along which `s`
becomes the value of *some* chart of the family form a Zariski covering sieve.

This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/

    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=

      Scheme.zariskiTopology T

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)

`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.

### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.

So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:

> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
> usually accompanies it.

This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
warning.

**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
their work and turns one incident into two.
